$note: A REWRITE STATION: the same shape as Reading/Database/templates/by_axis/json, sparse (only the fields this model wrote), never the truth. Adopt a field into the final template station with adopt.mjs on the owner's ruling.

angles.drive: Pressure is where your thinking gets clear and sure. Since nothing else makes you this sure of yourself, you take the hard version of a job ahead of the easy one. Once in a while pick a stake that is real rather than one you invented, because you think as well under those.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the pressure lifts, your focus goes with it, which is why a quiet week feels less like rest than like a punishment. You chase the next hard thing ahead of the sleep your body is asking for. Let the quiet week count as rest, since you need somewhere to come back from.
angles.cost_others: Bringing pressure into a calm place is something you do without noticing. Since you think better with stakes, you raise them for everyone near you rather than only for yourself. Save the stakes for the fights that need them, because you take a calm evening from the people at home each time you do.

angles.drive: Command comes to you before anyone hands it over. Standing by while a group drifts feels worse to you than being wrong out loud, so you take the decision ahead of the vote. Hand the next one over on purpose, because you lead better when you have chosen to.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you take the lead, you also take the weight that comes with it. You feel safer making a decision alone rather than sharing it, so you go too long without being carried yourself. Let one person in on the load, because you were never meant to hold yourself up alone.
angles.cost_others: Taking the decision off someone's hands is how you show care. Because waiting for the group feels like a risk you refuse, you decide ahead of the people who were about to. Leave the next call to them, since you take from the people you lead the chance to decide for themselves.

angles.drive: An ordinary week feels to you like being passed over. Because you only feel fully awake with something at risk, you pick the job with a chance of failing ahead of the safe one. Keep one of those going somewhere in your life, since you were built to be tested rather than kept safe.
angles.cost_self: Whenever life goes quiet, you feel like you are losing, which is why calm never feels like a reward to you. You spend rest as fast as it comes in, long before anyone asks. Let the quiet stretch be the prize rather than the gap, because you have one body to spend.
angles.cost_others: Raising the stakes is how you make a day feel real. Since an easy win bores you more than a hard loss, you turn plans that were working into tests they did not need to be. Keep the test for yourself, because you take the plain good day away from the people around you.

angles.drive: The hardest judge you answer to is the one inside you. Since any fight you cannot find outside goes looking for one within, you treat your own mistakes as crimes rather than as lessons. Remember that you never passed a test by punishing yourself for failing it.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you miss your standard, you start the punishment before anyone has seen the miss. You rarely decide rest has been earned, so you treat a day off as something to apologise for rather than something to take. You are the only judge who never leaves the house, and that is worth remembering.
angles.cost_others: Holding yourself to a hard standard is nothing you do in private. Since you give yourself no pass, you expect as much from the people close to you, and your silence after a mistake weighs more than shouting. Remember that you set the pressure at home as much as on yourself.

angles.drive: Your push arrives before your permission does. Because waiting for a yes feels like losing ground, you move people along ahead of asking whether the push was wanted. Keep in mind you bring the same force to a person that you bring to a problem.
angles.cost_self: Whenever you push, you spend strength you have not earned back, which is why you run empty sooner than you expect. You want to win the argument more than you want the energy to finish the week. Remember you are the one who pays for every push, and the bill comes in sleep.
angles.cost_others: Pushing people toward the answer is faster than walking them to it, and you choose fast. Since you trust force more than you trust patience, you teach the people near you to brace before you speak. Bear in mind you are harder to be close to than you are to follow.

angles.drive: Peace is the one order you never learned to take. Since you only feel safe while something is being handled, you keep a crisis going ahead of letting one end. Remember that you were made to win a fight rather than to stand guard after it.
angles.cost_self: Whenever the emergency ends, you go looking for the next one rather than lying down. You never fully take a rest you did not first defend, which is why tired has become your normal. Remember you have to call yourself off duty, since no order for it is coming.
angles.cost_others: Staying on duty is how you love the people you are responsible for. Since you keep watch instead of keeping company, you give them a guard ahead of someone to sit with. Remember you are hardest to reach when you are protecting someone the most.

angles.drive: Deciding fast is native wiring for you, and it reads as relief to everyone stuck deliberating. Options do not improve with age, in your experience, and your experience keeps proving it. The choice gets made while others are still framing the question. Then everyone breathes.
angles.cost_self: Twenty minutes into the dinner debate, you name the restaurant and stand up. Chairs scrape, coats go on, and the relief around the table is almost audible. Nobody remembers the other options by the sidewalk. Deciding was the meal everyone was actually hungry for.
angles.cost_others: People who deliberate for a living find your speed alarming until they work with it once. Then they start routing choices your way, quietly, the ones that have been circling for weeks. You settle them before lunch and nobody ever asks to reopen one.

angles.drive: Moving toward what others edge away from is wiring, and it spares you the weeks other people lose to dread. The feared thing shrinks on contact, every single time, and you have known that longer than most people have been avoiding their own versions of it.
angles.cost_self: The call everyone dreaded sat on your list for exactly one day. You made it standing up, between two other tasks, and it went the way these things usually go with you, which is fine. Three weeks of collective dread died in four unremarkable minutes.
angles.cost_others: Teams keep a mental list of things nobody wants to do, and your name has drifted next to most of them. Colleagues call it bravery to your face and something more useful behind your back: proof that the scary version of a task rarely survives contact with someone unafraid of it.

angles.drive: Emergencies make you calmer, which is rare enough that people remember it. Your talent switches on precisely when plans switch off: full clarity, short sentences, zero panic. Peace leaves you slightly restless, honestly. Collapse, oddly, brings out your very best manners.
angles.cost_self: The venue flooded at noon and the speaker cancelled at one. By ten past, you had a new hall, a new order of events, and a tone in your voice that made panic seem like a strange hobby other people had. The event ran. Nobody remembers how close it came.
angles.cost_others: There is a particular quiet that falls when things break and you are present, because everyone knows where the decisions will come from. It looks like glamour from a distance and it is really planning under pressure, done fast, and it has saved more days than anyone has counted.

angles.drive: Your intensity marks people whether you mean it or not, and you usually do not. The heat that cuts through problems does not distinguish problems from bystanders, and the bystanders remember longer. You forget the flare by lunch. Nobody standing near it ever does.
angles.cost_self: It was one word, sloppy, said at speed on a Tuesday and forgotten by lunch. A year later the person who caught it can still play it back with your exact inflection. You were putting out a fire. They were standing closer to it than you noticed.
angles.cost_others: New people get warned about you, gently, in hallways: brilliant, worth it, wear gloves. The warnings are affectionate and they are also warnings. Half the silence you read as respect is actually flinch, and the difference matters more every year you climb.

angles.drive: Taking charge is your reflex even where nobody asked, and mostly nobody asked. Any gathering without a commander strikes you as an emergency, and you fix it by quietly assuming the post. Order arrives on schedule. Volunteering, around you, just as quietly dies.
angles.cost_self: The vacation had a schedule by the first morning and a debrief by the last night, and somewhere in between, the group chat went quiet. One-word replies, thumbs up, fine. You ran a beautiful operation. The others were on holiday, or trying to be.
angles.cost_others: People under your command perform agreement long before they feel it, because pushing back costs more energy than most afternoons contain. Decisions that were never yours keep ending up yours. It feels like leadership from where you stand. From two steps away it looks like weather everyone dresses for.

angles.drive: Running at full flame until the fuel simply ends is a cycle for you, and calling it bad luck stopped working several cycles ago. The crash sits on the schedule now, as regular as the campaigns themselves. You just decline to read that far down.
angles.cost_self: The three months of heroics ended the way they always end, with two weeks where getting up felt like a rumor. From the couch you drafted apologies and, in the same hour, the next campaign. The pattern is so regular a friend once predicted your crash to within four days.
angles.cost_others: Everyone around you can see the crash coming except you, and they have learned not to say so out loud. They plan for your two dark weeks the way coastal towns plan for storm season, quietly moving what matters to higher ground. The storm never once takes the hint.

ledger: heavy Order on a weak body turns into the inner judge: pressure with no outside target lands on the self
force without permission: too much Order for the body, so the pressure goes outward onto whoever is near
peace felt as demotion, on the friction pole: the reader cannot stand down, so the crisis is kept alive
